reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds in the shared refunds table match the batch's requested refunds. I'll check the table first.
The refunds table matches the batch's requested refunds exactly (orders 220, 222, 223 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly, so there's no reason to hold. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, since it has two orders in the batch.

Acme's net balance is 25415. Its orders are 220 (33101) and 223 (24923), with refunds 9480 and 23129 in the table. Gross 58024 minus refunds 32609 is 25415, which matches the figure. Recording the payout for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, which has orders 221 and 224 in the batch. Its refunds are not in the requested list, so I'll get its net balance from the shared figure and pay it.

Birch has no refunds in the batch's requested list or the refunds table. Its net balance of 30973 matches its gross order total (19628 + 11345), so the figure is consistent. Recording the payout using the net_balance figure.

Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, with orders 222 (36677) and 225 (27011). Order 222 has a matching 30660 refund in the table. I'll get cobalt's net balance and check it against gross minus refunds before recording.
Cobalt's gross is 36677 + 27011 = 63688, and minus the matching 30660 refund gives 33028, which equals the net_balance figure. Recording the cobalt payout.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. Each refund in the batch matched the refunds table, and each payout was recorded once. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
